content.thinking: The replacement didn't apply (probably because the earlier replace changed the text? No...). Let me look: my replacement string had `m=copy.deepcopy(plan)\n    for a in range(K):` but the actual file has `m=copy.deepcopy(plan)` on line 69 presumably followed by `K=prof['groups']` on line 70. So the pattern didn't match. Let me patch with sed.

arguments.command:
cd /workspace/tmp && python3 - << 'PYEOF'
p='t2.py'; s=open(p).read()
s=s.replace("    if algo.audit(prof,fb,m)['valid']: print('BAD calib pred none'); bad+=1",
            "    if m!=plan and algo.audit(prof,fb,m)['valid']: print('BAD calib pred none'); bad+=1")
s=s.replace("    if algo.audit(prof,fb,m)['valid']: print('BAD calib pred shift (may be legit)'); ",
            "    if m!=plan and algo.audit(prof,fb,m)['valid']: print('note shift K=%d M=%d'%(K,len(prof['measurements']))); ")
open(p,'w').write(s)
PYEOF
grep -n "calib pred none\|note shift" t2.py && timeout 1800 python3 t2.py 3 40 && timeout 1800 python3 t2.py 11 80 2>&1|tail -8
